from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(speed_graph, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(velocity_label, "A3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00BFFF")
        tracer = Dot(color="#00BFFF", radius=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(tracer))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00BFFF")
        area = speed_graph.get_area(speed_graph.plot(lambda x: 2), color="#00BFFF", opacity=0.5)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Graphical Slope vs. Area", 
                         ["Recall the derivative represents the slope of the tangent.", 
                          "The integral represents the area under the curve.", 
                          "Both describe the same geometric function from different perspectives."])
        
        # Create mobjects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2 + 0.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # Tangent
        tangent_line = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#FF4500").scale(0.5)
        tangent_line.rotate(PI/4)
        tangent_line.move_to(axes.c2p(1.5, 0.5 * 1.5**2 + 0.5))
        
        # Area
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 2], color="#32CD32", opacity=0.5)
        
        # Place initially
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, curve), 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(tangent_line),
            FadeOut(area),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(curve)
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Integration is the reverse process of differentiation.",
            "Define the accumulation function as the area under curve.",
            "The rate of area growth equals the function height.",
            "This relationship forms the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.",
            "This bridge connects local change to total accumulation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Mechanism: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        func = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5, color=BLUE)
        area = axes.get_area(func, x_range=[0, 4], color=GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        label = MathTex("f(t)", color=BLUE).next_to(func, UP)
        
        visual_group = VGroup(axes, func, area, label)
        self.place_in_area(visual_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(func))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Create(area))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        v_line = Line(axes.c2p(4, 0), axes.c2p(4, func.underlying_function(4)), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(v_line))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        ftc = MathTex(r"\int_a^x f(t) dt = F(x) - F(a)", color=GOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(ftc, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(ftc))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.play(Indicate(ftc))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Think of differentiation and integration as inverse machines.",
            "Derivatives map a function to its rate of change.",
            "Integration maps the rate back to the original function.",
            "Constant C accounts for the starting point's ambiguity.",
            "These operations perfectly cancel each other out."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visual Synthesis: Inverse Operations", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define machine boxes
        box_diff = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.0, color=BLUE)
        label_diff = Text("Derivative", font_size=18).move_to(box_diff.get_center())
        machine_diff = VGroup(box_diff, label_diff)
        
        box_int = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1.0, color=GREEN)
        label_int = Text("Integral", font_size=18).move_to(box_int.get_center())
        machine_int = VGroup(box_int, label_int)

        self.place_at_grid(machine_diff, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(machine_int, 'E2')

        func_f = MathTex("f(x) = x^2", font_size=24)
        func_df = MathTex("f'(x) = 2x", font_size=24)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(machine_diff), FadeIn(machine_int))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(func_f, 'B1')
        self.play(FadeIn(func_f))
        self.play(func_f.animate.move_to(machine_diff.get_center()))
        self.play(FadeOut(func_f), FadeIn(func_df))
        self.place_at_grid(func_df, 'B3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(func_df.animate.move_to(machine_int.get_center()))
        self.play(FadeOut(func_df), FadeIn(func_f))
        self.place_at_grid(func_f, 'E3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        plus_c = MathTex("+ C", font_size=24, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(plus_c, 'E4')
        self.play(FadeIn(plus_c))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Indicate(machine_diff, color="#FF00FF"), Indicate(machine_int, color="#FF00FF"))

outline.topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Position Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the relationship through a real-world scenario. Use a 'Robot Runner' animation: the robot's speedometer (derivative) tells us its instantaneous speed, while the total distance covered (integral) is the accumulation of those speeds over time.
sections.example: If a robot moves at a constant speed of 2 m/s, the area under the speed-time graph (a rectangle) represents the total distance traveled.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Graphical Slope vs. Area
sections.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as the 'slope of the tangent line' and the definite integral as the 'area under the curve.' Visualize this by morphing a line into a shaded region on a Cartesian plane.
sections.example: Visualize the derivative as the steepness of a hill (tangent) and the integral as the total amount of soil needed to fill the valley (area).

sections.title: The Core Mechanism: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
sections.content: Explain that integration is the reverse process of differentiation. Present the 'Accumulation Function' F(x) = ∫f(t)dt from a to x. Show graphically how as x moves, the area grows at a rate proportional to the height of the function.
sections.example: If f(x) is the growth rate of a sunflower's height, the integral function F(x) represents the total height of the sunflower at day x.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis: Inverse Operations
sections.content: Use an animation showing an 'Operator Machine.' Inputting a function into the Derivative Machine produces the slope; inputting that slope back into the Integral Machine reconstructs the original function (plus a constant C).
sections.example: Input: Position function x(t) = t². Derivative Machine -> Velocity v(t) = 2t. Integral Machine -> Returns the original t² + C.

sections.title: Summary & Application Check
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing that derivatives measure 'change' (the slope) and integrals measure 'accumulation' (the area). These two processes are inverses, forming the backbone of engineering and physics.
sections.example: A smart thermostat tracks temperature change (derivative) to calculate total energy consumption (integral) for your smart home.
